playfulness relates positively to the Big Five traits of extraversion, lower agreeableness and lower conscientiousness; it is also related to greater endorsement of culture, greater joy of being laughed (gelotophilia), and greater intrinsic goal aspirations (and lower extrinsic goal aspirations).

playfulness in adults is related to extraversion and lower conscientiousness (Study 1), a high expectation of intrinsically and a low expectation for extrinsically motivated goals, as well as greater importance of intrinsic goals (Study 2), and greater self-perceived and psychometrically assessed ingenuity (Study 3).

playfulness relates positively to a variety of personality traits, positive psychological functioning and goal orientations.
the present study provides first evidence for the construct validity of playfulness in adulthood and its relation to personality, goal aspirations, psychological functioning, and creativity.

playfulness is related to a broad spectrum of personality traits and abilities, but that it is primarily related to a disposition to be more open to the world (extraversion, openness to experience, culture), to be less self-disciplined and self-controlled (conscientiousness), to be more agreeable (agreeableness), and to be more creative (self-perceptions of creativity as well as psychometric ingenuity).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
playfulness in adults is related to personality and ability measures in a meaningful and theoretically sound way.
playfulness, which is a disposition to play, relates positively to personality, positive psychological characteristics, and ability.
playfulness is a disposition to be more spontaneous and creative, to have a higher degree of openness to experience, and to have more fun.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a disposition to play in adults, which relates to personality, goal orientations and aspirations, and ingenuity.
playfulness is a multifaceted construct that is related to various aspects of personality and positive psychology.
playfulness is not just a child’s thing.
